name: theographic-bible-metadata
title: Theographic Bible Metadata
description: A knowledge graph of the Bible that links every verse of the King James Version to the people, places, events, people groups, and Easton's Bible Dictionary entries it mentions. Documentation: https://github.com/robertrouse/theographic-bible-metadata/tree/master/docs

sources.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), CCEL XML edition
Pleiades: A Gazetteer of Past Places
Floyd Nolen Jones, The Chronology of the Old Testament

fields.name: bookOrder

fields.name: bookName

fields.name: bookDiv

fields.description: Number of people mentioned by name within the book

fields.name: placeCount
fields.description: Number of places mentioned by name within the book

resources.name: people
resources.title: People
resources.description: Every individual named in the Bible (3,067 records), with family relationships, birth and death years and places, group membership, and the verses that mention them.

fields.name: personLookup
fields.description: Unique identifier using name and ID number

fields.name: personID
fields.description: Unique numerical identifier, helping to distinguish people with the same name.

fields.name: displayTitle
fields.description: Disambiguated name suitable for page titles and search results

fields.name: name
fields.description: Primary name used in the text of the KJV

fields.name: surname
fields.description: Surname, if known.

fields.name: alsoCalled
fields.description: Alternate spellings or other known names for the same person.

fields.name: isProperName
fields.description: Identifies those with proper names vs. descriptive names like "Wife of..." or "Son of..."

fields.name: ambiguous
fields.description: Identifies display titles which have not been edited for disambiguation.

fields.name: Disambiguation (temp)
fields.description: Mechanical Turk entries used to aid in disambiguation

fields.name: gender
fields.description: Male or Female

fields.name: birthYear
fields.description: Estimated birth year from Jones's chronology, as an ISO 8601 astronomical year in a numeric string (`"-4003"` = 4004 BC; `"-1570"` = 1571 BC; positive values are AD). Same convention as `events.startDate`. Populated for 70 people. See [Chronology and Dates](chronology-and-dates.md#people-dates).

fields.name: minYear
fields.description: Earliest year of the verses that mention this person (ISO 8601). Used to align people with the events timeline; not a birth year.

fields.name: deathYear
fields.description: Estimated death year, in the same convention as `birthYear` (`"-1014"` = 1015 BC). Populated for 61 people.

fields.name: maxYear
fields.description: Latest year of the verses that mention this person (ISO 8601).

fields.name: deathPlace

fields.name: memberOf

fields.name: eastons

fields.name: dictText

fields.name: eastons

fields.name: dictText
fields.description: Markdown-formatted text from relevant sub-section in Easton's dictionary. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: recogitoLat

fields.name: recogitoType

fields.name: booksWritten

fields.name: eventsHere
fields.description: An array of record IDs linking to the 'events' table, representing events that occurred at this location. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: hasBeenHere
fields.description: A string containing a comma-separated list of `personLookup` identifiers for people who have visited this location.

fields.name: latitude
fields.description: Best available latitude, chosen from Recogito and OpenBible validation. Stored as a string; convert to a number before mapping. Present on 1,272 place records.

fields.name: longitude
fields.description: Best available longitude, depending on Recogito and OpenBible validation

fields.name: alphaGroup
fields.description: Used for alphabetical indexing

fields.name: slug
fields.description: Lowercase, url-friendly version of placeLookup

fields.name: canonicalPlace
fields.description: The record ID of the place record this record is another name for (e.g. Salem → Jerusalem). Empty on the canonical record and on places with only one name. Each record keeps its own verses, so each name keeps its own time frame. Replaces `rootID` and `duplicate_of`, retired 2026-10-13 (values archived on the [`geo-pipeline`](https://github.com/robertrouse/theographic-bible-metadata/tree/geo-pipeline/geo/airtable) branch). In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: otherNames
fields.description: On a canonical record, the records that point to it via `canonicalPlace` (the other names of this place). In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: partOf
fields.description: Record IDs of the places this place lies within: a city's tribal territory (Joshua's allotment lists), a site's city (gates of Jerusalem), a city's Roman region, a territory's kingdom. A place can be part of several (Zorah: Dan and Judah). Set on canonical records. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: parts
fields.description: On a containing place, the records whose `partOf` points to it. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: near
fields.description: Record IDs of places this place lies beside or just outside (Gethsemane → Jerusalem). In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: nearby
fields.description: On a place, the records whose `near` points to it. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: startYear
fields.description: For a place that existed only for a period, such as a kingdom, its first year (ISO astronomical: -1094 = 1095 BC). Dates every `partOf` link to it.

fields.name: endYear
fields.description: That place's last year, same numbering.

resources.name: events
resources.title: Events
resources.description: A timeline of 450 biblical events with dates, durations, predecessors, participants, locations, and verses. Old Testament and Gospel dates follow Floyd Nolen Jones; Acts dates follow Todd Atwood. Years are ISO 8601 astronomical years (-4003 = 4004 BC).

fields.name: title
fields.description: Unique title for an event

fields.name: eventID
fields.description: Unique identifier

fields.name: startDate
fields.description: An ISO 8601 astronomical year (`"-4003"` = 4004 BC) or calendar date (`"0030-04-04"`). Present on every event.

fields.name: duration
fields.description: Event length: a number plus `D`, `W`, `M`, or `Y` (e.g. `"7D"`, `"40Y"`)

fields.name: predecessor
fields.description: An array containing the record ID of the immediately preceding event in the timeline. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: lag
fields.description: Time between the predecessor event and this one, in the same format as `duration` (e.g. `"130Y"`).

fields.name: lagType
fields.description: The type of predecessor relationship - either Start-to-Start (SS) or Finish-to-Start (FS). For example, for an event with lag of 130Y, lagType `FS` means that the event started 130 years after the predecessor event finished, whereas lagType `SS` means that the event started 130 years after the predecessor event started.

fields.name: partOf
fields.description: An array containing the record ID of a parent event, indicating this event is a sub-component of a larger narrative arc. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: verses
fields.description: An array of record IDs linking to the 'verses' table, representing the scriptural basis for the event. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: participants
fields.description: An array of record IDs linking to the 'people' table, representing the participants in the event. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: locations
fields.description: An array of record IDs linking to the 'places' table, representing the location(s) where the event occurred. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: groups
fields.description: An array of record IDs linking to the 'peopleGroups' table, representing groups involved in the event. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: notes
fields.description: A field for additional commentary or explanatory notes about the event.

fields.name: verseSort
fields.description: The `verseID` of the first verse in the `verses` field of this event.

fields.name: modified
fields.description: Last modified date and time

fields.name: sortKey
fields.description: Uses a combination of year and verseSort to sort all events chronologically. The calculation formula, originated in airtable, is `INT(IF(LEFT(startDate,1)='-',LEFT(startDate,5),LEFT(startDate,4))) + INT(verseSort)/100000000`

resources.name: easton
resources.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary
resources.description: Entries from Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), parsed from the CCEL XML edition and linked to people and places.

fields.name: dictLookup
fields.description: Unique string for a dictionary entry, split out by sub-paragraphs

fields.name: index
fields.description: Unique identifier

fields.name: termID
fields.description: This field preserves the term’s original position in the source XML, making theographic’s extraction process transparent and allowing easy entry to trace back to its source context. It records the `id` attribute of the `<term>` tag in the source XML, and it indicates the location of the term within the original document's structure. For example, `a-p1.11` signifies that the term is in the "a" section, and that, within that section, it is associated with the paragraph block indexed as "p1", and that within that block, it is the 11th tagged element.

fields.name: termLabel
fields.description: The title of the dictionary term being defined.

fields.name: dictText
fields.description: The full definition text for the term. This field may contain Markdown-style links and newline characters for paragraph breaks.

fields.name: itemNum
fields.description: Indicates the item number for definitions that are part of a list (e.g., 1, 2, 3). This occurs when multiple definitions exist for the same word and they are itemized. Defaults to 0 for entries that are not itemized.

fields.name: matchType
fields.description: Used to validate scripts which automatically match entities.

fields.name: matchSlugs
fields.description: Used to check automatically matched slugs of entities in other tables

fields.name: personLookup
fields.description: An array of record IDs that link to corresponding entries in the 'people' JSON. Each ID represents a person mentioned in the dictText. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: placeLookup
fields.description: An array of record IDs that link to corresponding entries in the 'places' JSON. Each ID represents a place mentioned in the dictText. In the CSV this is a comma-separated list of lookup values (e.g. personLookup, placeLookup, osisRef) rather than record IDs.

fields.name: Chapter
fields.description: Chapter number.

fields.name: VerseID
fields.description: Sequential verse number.

fields.name: VerseNum

fields.name: Word

fields.name: Punc
fields.description: Punctuation following the word.

fields.name: Italic

fields.name: PlaceID
fields.description: placeID of the place this word refers to, or 0.

fields.name: Syllables

fields.name: YearNum
